title: Unramified algebra maps descend along directed colimits
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and let $A=\varinjlim_{i\in I}A_i$ be a directed colimit of commutative rings. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a map of $A_{i_0}$-algebras $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$. Put $B_i=A_i\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0$, $C_i=A_i\otimes_{A_{i_0}}C_0$, and $B=A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0$, $C=A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}C_0$. Assume that $B\to C$ is unramified as a ring map, meaning that $C$ is a finitely generated $B$-algebra and its module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{C/B}$ is zero [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and assume that $C_0$ is a finitely generated $B_0$-algebra. Then there exists $i\ge i_0$ such that $B_i\to C_i$ is unramified: $C_i$ is finitely generated over $B_i$ and $\Omega_{C_i/B_i}=0$.
